title: Money Format: Consistent USD, Dates, and Card Display
audience: Frontend developers and designers learning the Clear Mint midnight-ledger restyle
objectives: Understand why consistent formatting across dashboard, card history, add-money, and snap-bill offer builds trust
Use formatCurrency correctly for USD balances, caps, and amounts without changing wording
Apply formatCapUsage for spent-vs-cap and formatPercent for rates with consistent presentation
Apply formatDate for due and charge dates and maskCardNumber for safe display
Distinguish charge versus decline wording with formatTxnResult while keeping feature wording identical

designContext.lightAiryMint: Clear Mint midnight-ledger restyle only uses light airy mint tokens for a fresh ledger feel, with tinted and dark LedgerBand variants and restyled home and dashboard panels, while formatting helpers keep wording identical
designContext.typefaces: Space Grotesk is used for display headings and Figtree for body text, preserving readability across all formatted money and date surfaces
designContext.softCards: Panels use 14px soft cards with soft rounded corners and subtle elevation to frame balances, history, and offers in the midnight-ledger layout

pitch30s: Welcome to Money Format, your guide to how every dollar, date, and card number looks the same everywhere in the app. You'll learn how formatCurrency keeps USD consistent, formatCapUsage shows spent versus cap, formatDate stamps due dates clearly, maskCardNumber protects privacy, formatPercent clarifies rates, and formatTxnResult tells charges from declines. Same wording, cleaner Mint ledger look with soft cards and clear type. Let's make money language simple and trustworthy.

analogies.title: Price Tags in Every Aisle
analogies.explanation: formatCurrency is like using the same price-tags in every store aisle: dashboard, card history, add-money, and snap-bill offer all show USD balances, caps, and amounts with identical USD writing so users instantly trust the value.

analogies.title: Calendar Stamp for Due Dates
analogies.explanation: formatDate works like a clear calendar-stamp that marks due and charge dates the same way every time, so you never misread when payment is due.

analogies.title: Redacted Letter for Card Safety
analogies.explanation: maskCardNumber is like a redacted letter where a masked-card-as-redacted-letter hides sensitive digits and shows only the last four, keeping display safe while still identifiable.

concepts: formatCurrency for USD balances, caps, and amounts ensures consistent USD writing across dashboard, card history, add-money, and snap-bill offer
formatCapUsage for spent-vs-cap builds on formatCurrency to show progress toward a cap with identical amount formatting
formatDate for due and charge dates provides consistent date writing across all ledger surfaces
maskCardNumber for safe display masks card numbers for privacy while preserving recognizability
formatPercent formats percentages and rates consistently alongside currency values

formatTxnResult for charge vs decline wording distinguishes successful charges from declines, emphasizing consistency across dashboard, card history, add-money, and snap-bill offer while keeping wording identical

quizzes.question: How should a USD balance of 1234.5 appear when using formatCurrency?
quizzes.explanation: formatCurrency uses standard USD writing with dollar sign, comma grouping, and two decimal places for all balances, caps, and amounts.

quizzes.question: Which example shows correct date writing for a charge date using formatDate?
quizzes.explanation: formatDate provides clear, human-readable date writing like May 9, 2025 for due and charge dates.

quizzes.question: How should a declined transaction appear using formatTxnResult?
choices: Declined with distinct decline wording separate from a charge
Identical to a successful charge with no distinction
Shown as zero amount with no status
quizzes.explanation: formatTxnResult keeps charge vs decline wording distinct so users can immediately tell a decline from a successful charge while wording stays consistent.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Motion for soft cards and LedgerBand transitions respects reduced motion preferences with minimal animation and no auto-playing movement.
accessibility.keyboard: All panels, balances, and history entries remain fully keyboard accessible with visible focus states, allowing navigation of dashboard, card history, add-money, and snap-bill offer without a mouse.
